findings.issue: Domain services have no read path. §4 says every write class 'also requires the row's read predicate for the session', and read classes give service or write_service sessions nothing extra. Yet §7 requires a balanced svc-ledger journal to commit inside an investor or agent session. That journal touches platform-tenant offer_escrow entries the investor cannot read. G07 holder-cap totals, offering raise totals, escrow balances and A16 availability checks all need rows of other people inside the person's transaction. withSystem accounts without platform_access (svc-agent-access writing last_used_at, the A12 expiry sweep, the A40 run jobs) read nothing either, because class 1 gives 'service' sessions nothing. The builder must either break the stated rule or weaken RLS.
findings.fix: State that P writes through withDomainWrite are checked against WRITE_SERVICES, not the session read predicate. Add a matching service-read extension: app.write_service also grants SELECT on the tables that WRITE_SERVICES/READ_SERVICES list for that service. Alternatively, put aggregates (holder totals, raise totals, account balances) behind SECURITY DEFINER functions listed in DEFINER_GRANTS. Say which service_account rows get which access, including svc-agent-access. Add tests for an investor-session order that funds escrow, a G07 total across holders and an A12 sweep under withSystem.

findings.issue: The database blocks acts that A12, A03 and D04 make delegable or passkey-free. refuse_agent_write covers api_token, agent_mandate and wallet_key with no carve-out, so a token cannot revoke itself. A12 §2 allows this, and A03 says 'revoke stays delegable so an agent can kill itself'. agent_mandate.assertion_id is NOT NULL and every change inserts a new version, so narrowing by a signed-in owner without a passkey (A12 line 101) and narrowing by the token's own bearer are impossible. Token rotation also needs a fresh assertion under A12, but api_token has no column to bind it.
findings.fix: Add explicit, listed carve-outs. Allow an agent session whose app.token_id = api_token.id to move state to revoked, and write revoked_at, revoked_by and revoke_reason, only on its own row. Allow a new agent_mandate version without an assertion when a trigger proves it is a strict subset of its predecessor (scopes, caps, vehicles, windows, expiry). Make assertion_id required only for creation and widening. Allow the session-key revocation rows on self-revoke. Add rotated_with_assertion_id and have api_token_no_inplace_widening also treat a secret_hash change as needing it. Add probes: self-revoke succeeds, self-widen is refused, owner narrow without passkey succeeds, owner widen without passkey is refused.

findings.issue: The approval binding model contradicts A38 and A18. A38 F5 has one allocation.mint approval (object_ref = allocation_id) bind the register instruction, the custody op and the chain tx. A04 makes register_instruction of kind issue privileged and requires approval object_ref = '<table>:<objectRefColumn>', which for this row is 'register_instruction:...', and a partial UNIQUE(approval_id). A18 needs UNIQUE(approval_id, kind), so one approval can cover issue and redeem, and it keeps certification approvals on its registered register_certification, not register_version. So A04's oracle (h) forces the mint pipeline and the register to fail, or the builder loosens the trigger.
findings.fix: In PRIVILEGED_TABLES, let each table declare the object its approval names as a (type, column) pair, not '<table>:<col>'. For example, register_instruction(issue) binds 'allocation:<reference.allocation_id>'. Replace the per-table UNIQUE(approval_id) with the uniqueness key each shaping node fixes: UNIQUE(approval_id, kind) for register_instruction. Adopt A18's request that register_version carries no approval and certification lives on register_certification, or record the decision in §2 and flag A18. Add an A38-shaped legitimate case to (h) and the Approval binding suite.

findings.issue: A09, the direct AM0 dependent, cannot release an idempotency claim. A09 deletes the in_progress idempotency_key row under realx_app when the business transaction rolls back. A04's hard-delete trigger allows deletes on idempotency_key only for realx_worker on rows past expires_at. A04 also makes expires_at NOT NULL, but A09 sets it only at completion. A09's crash and concurrency oracle then fails at A04's trigger.
findings.fix: Pick one. (a) Allow realx_app to DELETE an idempotency_key row only when state = 'in_progress', claim_token matches a transaction-local app.claim_token, and the row is the session's own (class 8). (b) Add a 'released' state that A09 sets instead of deleting, and flag A09. Set expires_at at claim time (lease plus 24 h). Add a test for claim, rollback, release and re-claim under realx_app.

findings.issue: The Ownership pass criterion fails by construction at A04's gate. It says 'every table named in any node spec resolves to exactly one row of TABLE_OWNERS'. The Challenge says conflicts are findings against the other spec, so the two rules contradict. Many names do not resolve today: A11 still registers fresh_assertion itself (A04 makes it core, and the registry refuses the clash); mandate_usage appears in A17, A29, A82, A83 and A101; A16 has ledger_payout; A18 has register_certification and register_freeze_fact; A38 has settlement_run and settlement_step; outbox_event appears in A09, A44, A46 and A85. A09 also still routes runtime SVCA work through withPlatform, where A04 requires withSystem with runtime_access, and A10 still lists A04's old columns and four principal types.
findings.fix: Rewrite the criterion so A04 passes when every name either resolves in ownership.json or is recorded in A04.qa.md as a finding against the named spec. Add an alias list (outbox_event -> outbox, mandate_usage -> agent_counter) to ownership.json. Pre-register the known future registry tables with their owning node (ledger_payout, register_certification, register_freeze_fact, settlement_run, settlement_step and so on) as 'planned registry' rows. Raise edits for A11 (drop fresh_assertion from its registry list), A09 (withSystem), A10 (current column list, AGTU) and the mandate_usage specs.

findings.issue: The step-up assertion lifecycle is inconsistent. A11's nonce-mode middleware and its inline mode 'consume the row' themselves. A04's assertion_binding_check sets consumed_* and refuses a row 'already set by another row or by another transaction', and neither spec defines the handshake. The generic realx_insert_only function 'refuses any DELETE for every role', but fresh_assertion (RUNTIME_PURGEABLE) and audit_event (the sandbox purger) must allow sanctioned deletes. The pass criteria require 100% of DELETEs on insert-only tables under all four login roles to raise and also require realx_worker to purge. Nonce rows are referenced by assertion rows through nonce_id, so purging an expired nonce breaks the FK.
findings.fix: Define the handshake. A11's verifier inserts the assertion with consumed_* null in the business transaction, and the binding trigger sets consumed_at, consumed_txid and consumed_by_ref; or A11 sets consumed_txid, the trigger accepts it only when it equals pg_current_xact_id() and consumed_by_ref is null, and then fills it. Give realx_insert_only a purge-exception parameter used only by the hard-delete rules. Purge only nonce rows no assertion references (or make nonce_id ON DELETE SET NULL after consumption). Qualify the immutability pass criterion with the sanctioned purges.

findings.issue: A pending token can become active without its second person. The only floor is CHECK NOT(state IN (active, held) AND pending_expires_at IS NOT NULL AND no cosigner, approver or approval), and pending_expires_at is not immutable. An UPDATE that sets state = 'active' and pending_expires_at = NULL in one statement passes the CHECK. The cosigner's assertion is also not bound to the same payload hash as the creator's (A12: 'over the same payload hash').
findings.fix: Add an immutable column second_person_required (none | cosign | owner_approval) set at insert, and CHECK that an active or held token with a requirement has the matching assertion or approval. Make pending_expires_at set-once. In ASSERTION_COLUMNS, require cosigner and approver assertions to carry the payload_sha256 of the creation assertion. Add a probe that clears pending_expires_at while activating.

findings.issue: Custody ops can bind during the veto window. APPROVAL_BINDABLE_STATES is 'every state reachable from approved that is not a failure or pending state', which includes A03's SM-00 extension state queued (timelock and veto window, 48 h for forced transfer and recovery). So a custody_op can be bound, and signed, before the veto window ends. The test also names 'vetoed', which is not an A03 SM-00 state (veto moves to cancelled).
findings.fix: Give custody_op its own bindable set: queued_for_custody and later, never queued. Keep queued bindable only where the business row must exist before the timelock. Generate the excluded list from A03's export and drop 'vetoed'. Add a probe: bind a custody_op to an approval in queued, which must be refused.

findings.issue: Class 2 on the ledger has no key column. Class 2 is investor_id = app.investor_id, and §2 says investor cash accounts 'carry investor_id'. A16's ledger_account has owner_ref and no investor_id, and ledger_entry has beneficiary_id and no investor_id. An investor's own escrow legs sit on offer_escrow accounts (owner = the offering), with beneficiary_id = the investor, and they are what the investor must read for 'In offer escrow'. The generated class-2 test cannot be written against a column the spec never fixes.
findings.fix: Fix the columns in §2. Add ledger_account.investor_id, derived from owner_ref for investor_cash by CHECK. Add ledger_entry.investor_id, set by a SECURITY DEFINER trigger to the account's investor_id, or to beneficiary_id when beneficiary_id is an investor. Make class 2 on ledger_entry use that column. Add X/Y tests over investor_cash and offer_escrow legs.
